about.summary: A free, open-source editor for learning Python. Your code stays on this computer.
about.button_title: Open the About group, with the credits list you can edit.
app.description: A fully accessible IDE for dyslexic and neurodivergent learners.
app.title: AccessibleCoding - Code comfortably
brand.name: AccessibleCoding

footer.text: AccessibleCoding - built with empathy for dyslexic and neurodivergent learners.
glass.help: These are a look, not a legibility aid. If the softened edges or the extra colour make anything harder to pick out, choose None (solid).
glass.material_help: How solid the bars and panels around your code are. Your code itself always stays solid, so the contrast you read by does not change. Mica is quiet and nearly solid. Frosted is an even blur. Acrylic is the heaviest and most see-through, with a faint grain.
glass.tint_help: Blends with the colour your theme already uses, so it shifts the panels' colour without losing the theme's contrast. Leave it empty to follow the theme. Type a hex colour such as #223344.
glass.tint_picker_label: Choose a colour for the panels

glossary.title: Python dictionary
keys.hint: Running the code always uses Enter with another key held down. Stopping always uses Escape, either pressed twice or with another key held down. Enter on its own still starts a new line, and Escape on its own still closes a box, so neither of them is ever used alone.
keys.recording: Press the keys now, or Escape to cancel
keys.rejected: That key press is not one this app can use. Choose one from the list instead.
keys.stop: Stop the program that is running
language.help: This changes the words in AccessibleCoding. Your code stays the same.
language.label: Language
layout.editor_divider: Resize the editor and the output
layout.shell_divider: Resize the output and the shell
motion.help: Turning this on stops the buttons, switches and panels moving. Nothing disappears, it just arrives straight away.
motion.hint: Movement is extra. Turning it off never changes what the app does, only how quickly things arrive.
motion.label: Reduce motion
nav.save_title: Save your code to a file

python.AttributeError: You're trying to use an attribute or method that doesn't exist on this object.
python.FileNotFoundError: The file you're trying to open doesn't exist.
python.ImportError: Python can't find the module you're trying to import.
python.IndentationError: Indentation error. Python uses spaces to group code blocks. Make sure your indentation is consistent.
python.IndexError: You're trying to access an index that doesn't exist in a list or string.
python.KeyError: You're trying to access a dictionary key that doesn't exist.
python.MemoryError: Your program ran out of memory.
python.ModuleNotFoundError: The module you're trying to import isn't installed.
python.NameError: You're using a variable or function name that hasn't been defined yet.
python.PermissionError: You don't have permission to access this file.
python.RecursionError: Your function is calling itself too many times (infinite recursion).
python.SyntaxError: There's a syntax error in your code. Check for missing parentheses, brackets, or quotes.
python.TabError: This line mixes tabs and spaces at the start, so Python cannot tell how far it is indented.
python.TypeError: You're trying to do something with the wrong type of data (like adding text to a number).
python.ValueError: A function received a value of the right type but an inappropriate value.
python.ZeroDivisionError: You're dividing by zero, which isn't allowed.
python.mistake.assignment: A single = saves a value. In an if or while line you are comparing two values, so use ==.
python.mistake.bad_dedent: This line is not indented the same way as the block it looks like it belongs to.
python.mistake.extra_bracket: The {0} closes a bracket that was never opened. Check the brackets in this line and remove the extra one.
python.mistake.missing_colon: This line needs a colon at the end.
python.mistake.missing_indent: The line after this one needs to be indented, because it belongs to this block.
python.mistake.tabs_and_spaces: This line starts with tabs and spaces mixed together. Use one or the other.
python.mistake.text_and_number: Text and a number cannot be joined like this. Put int() or str() around one of them so both sides are the same kind of value.
python.mistake.unclosed_bracket: The {0} bracket was opened and never closed. Every opening bracket needs its closing partner.
python.mistake.unclosed_quote: A quote mark was opened and never closed, so Python is still reading the rest of the line as text.
python.mistake.unexpected_indent: This line is indented further than the line above it.
python.mistake.unknown_name: Python does not know the name "{0}". Check the spelling, or give it a value before this line.
python.mistake.unknown_name_suggestion: Python does not know the name "{0}". Did you mean "{1}"?
quit.body: Your code and settings stay on this computer. Quitting closes the editor window.
quit.title: Quit AccessibleCoding?
quit.unsaved_note: You have changes that are not saved yet. Save your work before you quit.
reading.font_weight_help: How heavy the letters look. 400 is normal; higher is bolder.
reading.hint: These change how the code looks. Nothing here needs a restart.
reading.letter_spacing_help: Extra space between letters. Some readers find a little more easier to track.
reading.line_height_help: How much space between lines. More space can make text easier to follow.
reading.ruler_help: A shaded band follows your pointer so one line stays easy to follow. The keyboard and the caret are unchanged.
reading.upload_font_help: Choose a .ttf, .otf, .woff or .woff2 file from your computer.
settings.not_saved: Changed for now. It will not be remembered until the app is back online.
settings.reset_help: Puts every setting back to the default. Your code is not touched.
settings.save_failed: That setting could not be saved.
settings.title: Settings
setup.custom_advanced: Code colours for keywords, strings, comments, numbers and functions are in Settings, under Colours, Advanced.
setup.custom_help: Pick a colour from the grid, or type a hex code. Each choice is checked against the background as you make it.
setup.error_saved: We could not save that. Please try again.
setup.font_help: Pick a font from the list. The line under it shows how it looks.
setup.label: First-time setup
setup.language_help: You can change this at any time in {0}.
setup.skip: Skip this and use the defaults
setup.theme_custom: Custom - choose your own colours on the next screen.
setup.theme_help: Pick the colours you will look at all day. You can change them later in Settings.
setup.title: Let's set up AccessibleCoding
setup.tour_editor_text: Type Python in the box on the left. Take as long as you like.
setup.tour_run_text: Press {0}, or {1}, to see what your code does.
setup.tour_settings_text: Change the colours, spacing, focus mode and voice in {0}.

shell.clear_title: Forget everything you have typed in the shell
shell.closed: The Python shell stopped. It has been started again for you.
shell.no_code: There is nothing to run yet. Type something first.
shell.no_session: The Python shell is not open. Open it and try again.
shell.restarted: The Python shell was started again, so what you had typed earlier is gone.
shell.timeout: That took too long, so it was stopped. Look for a loop that never ends.
shell.title: Python Shell
sound.help: A short sound when your code starts, finishes, fails or waits for an answer, and a soft click on buttons. Turn this off if sound distracts you.
sound.label: Sound effects
speak.click: Read a label when I click it
speak.click_help: Clicking a button, a heading or a label says what it is. Your code and the results window are left alone, so running your program still behaves normally.
speak.demo: This is how your code results will sound when they are read aloud.
speak.help: When this is on, AccessibleCoding reads the output and any error message out loud after you run your code.
speak.hover_all: Everything, including the text on the page
speak.hover_areas: Read these when I point at them
speak.hover_areas_help: Pointing at one of these reads that part aloud after the pause above. Each stays off until you ask for it, so nothing is read out that you did not want.
speak.hover_delay_help: A short pause before each one. A longer wait means hovering only speaks when you rest on something, rather than every time the pointer passes over it.
speak.hover_scope_help: How much of the screen is worth reading out loud. This sits alongside your own screen reader rather than replacing it.
speak.rate_help: Around 1 is a normal speaking pace. Below 1 is slower.
speak.voice_gender_help: Your computer does not say which voices are male or female, so this is a best guess made from the voice names. Picking a voice yourself above overrides it, and the app uses whatever is installed on this computer.
speak.voice_help: The voices here come from your computer and Windows. Not every computer has the same ones.
theme.advanced_help: Keywords, strings, comments, numbers and functions. The stored values already pass the contrast check, so change these only if you want to.
theme.custom_contrast_fail: Hard to read on this background.
theme.custom_help: Build your own theme. Every colour is checked against the background as you pick it.
theme.gradient_help: A soft wash of colour behind the editor. Turn it off if it bothers you.
trace.button_title: Show what each line did to your variables
trace.empty: This run did not set or change any variables.
trace.heading: What each line did
trace.hint: A row appears each time a value changes, on the line that changed it.
trace.not_run_yet: Run your code first. The trace table describes your last run.
trace.truncated: Showing the first {0} of {1} steps. Shorter programs fit in one table.
try.error_not_hex: That is not a colour. Use # followed by 3 or 6 letters or digits, like #ffd93d.
try.highlight_help: The colour behind the line you are working on. Leave it empty to use the theme colour.
try.hint: See how your font and colour look before you keep them. Everything here is saved straight away.
try.nudge_help: If a colour would be hard to read on your theme, the app nudges it until it is easy to read again.
try.picker_label: Pick a colour with the colour picker
try.sample_default: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
try.sample_help: Change the words to anything you like. The preview below follows along.
try.status_nudged: On this theme it was lightened or darkened to {0} so it stays easy to read.
try.system_font: {0} comes from your computer. If it does not show, an included font will be used instead.
update.auto_check_help: The app looks once a day when you open it. It only tells you a new version exists; you decide what happens next.
update.channel_beta: Beta - new work, released often. Small problems are more likely.
update.channel_help: Beta gets every new version as soon as it is ready. Stable waits for a large, finished change. This app is on Beta now, so Stable may have nothing newer for a long time.
update.channel_stable: Stable - big finished changes, released less often.
update.check_help: Ask for a new version straight away, whether or not the automatic check is on.
update.error_bad_manifest: The update information could not be read, so nothing was changed.
update.error_bad_url: The download address was not accepted, so nothing was downloaded.
update.error_bad_version: The version number in the update information could not be read.
update.error_channel_empty: Nothing has been published on this channel yet. You are up to date with the newest build, and there is nothing to download.
update.error_checked_recently: Already checked a little while ago.
update.error_checksum: The downloaded file was not what was expected, so it was discarded and nothing was changed.
update.error_download_failed: The download did not finish, so nothing was changed.
update.error_missing_build: The new version's file is missing.
update.error_network: Could not reach GitHub to check for updates. Your work is unaffected.
update.error_no_checksum: The new version came without a safety check, so it was not downloaded.
update.error_no_update: There is no newer version to install, so nothing was changed.
update.error_not_applicable: Updates only apply to the downloaded desktop app.
update.error_prepare: The update could not be prepared. Close the app and try again.
update.error_start: The update could not be started. Close the app and try again.
update.error_too_large: The file is bigger than expected, so it was not downloaded.
update.error_unknown: The update check did not work. Nothing was changed.
update.hint: New versions are published on GitHub. Nothing is downloaded or changed without your asking.
update.install_help: The new version is checked before it is used. You can install it straight away with the button that appears after the download, or it goes in place when you close the app.
update.restart_help: Closes the app, puts the new version in place, and opens the app again.
update.status_applying: Installing the update. The app will close and open again.
update.status_current: You are on the newest version ({0}).
update.status_downloading: Downloading the new version. This can take a minute.
update.status_not_applicable: This is the website version, so it updates by itself when the site is updated.
update.status_off: Automatic checking is off. You can still ask at any time.
update.status_ready: Version {0} is downloaded and ready to install.
update.warn_body: Downloading only saves the new version; nothing changes yet. Installing closes the app, puts the new version in place, and opens the app again, so save anything you have not saved.
